title: Dikhit — 'The Informational Role of the Most Recent Month in Industry-Level Momentum Strategies' (Zenodo preprint, Jan 2026) — skip-month is not universally beneficial; carries signal conditional on last month's return
rationale: Tests 12-1 vs 12-0 momentum on Fama-French 48 industries, 1975-2024. Finds the skip-month (conventionally excluded to dodge short-term reversal) actually carries signal: when the most recent month's return was above-average, subsequent momentum performance was stronger, contradicting the standard reversal-driven justification for skipping it unconditionally. Directly engages our own H277 anomaly (skip-month *hurts* on NASDAQ tech momentum, OOS Sharpe 1.22 without skip vs worse with it) by giving a theoretical/industry-level mechanism for why unconditional skip-month isn't universally correct. Concrete, well-scoped follow-up: a 'conditional skip' variant (skip only when last month's return was below-average) tested on the H198/H417/H490 momentum universes. Not previously ingested. Caveat: Zenodo preprint, not arXiv or peer-reviewed -- lower-tier source, treat findings as directional pending replication on our own universes.
